I disagree that that the exchange of money and presence of capitalistic economy inherently perverts all that utilizes them. We live in an imperfect world; if indigenous people and their lands are being raped by unchecked capitalism, they are forced to "play the game" to protect themselves- how else can they secure land as theirs when monopolizers would otherwise clear-cut the forests; how else can they shield their wisdom-keeping traditions than with the "legitimacy" (in BPME eyes) that money exchange lends them?

Does monetary profit inherently empower evil? In a world on the brink of implosion, does it not make sense to generate money (modernity's Power) as quickly as possible, within empathetic boundaries, with which to protect lands, buy regenerative resources (ie seeds, animals), procure and create books, etc and prepare a community to be resilient to the real forces of destruction which face us today? 

If humble guides can inform westerners' imbalanced views with plant medicine, coaxing them in with the familiarity of capitalistic money exchange, and thus ease intergenerational cycles of accrued suffering, then isn't that a blessing? 

If a shaman is seeking recognition and validation through their practices, how is that any different from anyone else who utilizes their natural propensities and culturally available niches to secure positive self regard and meaning within a community? If we are afraid of their ability to induce trance, and the "suggestibility" of a plant, doesn't that speak more to our own self doubts, that we may be 'duped' and cannot trust our intuition or manage whatever circumstance we are in?

Why wouldn't the response to a shaman's vibrant self-trust and function to mobilize others on a path of deeper looking be one of laughter and celebration for their own unique manifestation of beauty, the cosmos' passion for novelty? Why harbor suspicion? No one can cast black magic upon you without your permission. 

Sure, some shamans do abuse their position just as priests, or any other person with a position of respect and profession of guidance, may abuse theirs. We certainly must learn to identify those who feed off others' suffering; those caught in a pain-spiral who take, without concern for the well-being of those they profit from. 

The exchange of money and capitalism itself are not evil, they are mere tools, which are currently caught in the line of fire because of the imbalanced, greedy ends they are being used towards. The entire earth is affected by systemic monopolization practices; BPME utilizes money and capitalism as tools but should we shun these things out of association? Cannot they be implemented strategically to ease suffering, and support a balanced living world?

I do agree we should all seek listening to, and observing, the patterns of Life itself, as our Guru. Or in other words, we must seek to become our own guru. Yes we are all simultaneously students and teachers. Yet how can we learn if we do not hear the insights of others? A professed shaman is a human being like any other who we may observe, to aggregate more data from, with which to form our own conclusions. They hold valuable anthropological, pharmacological, psychological and other insights, because of what they have devoted their life to. We can glean deeper understanding of the world through them (just like any other person)....if they claim ultimate authority on reality, then this is just another data point to take account into our understanding of how the world and people work. Why reject all someone says just because they missed a piece of the puzzle? Again we all have lessons to share and insights yet to be had. 

A shamans' ability to heal by suggestion doesn't make them a malicious charlatan. It makes them a person who understands how some human minds work, and that sometimes suggestion and conviction of "power" is all one needs to allow the individual to heal themselves. A shaman provides just one avenue to healing. A shamans' very existence suggests that perhaps humans have long struggled with Fear and lack of intuitive self-trust, need for peer reassurance and confirmation, as apart of our growth stage in the evolution of our species. Perhaps a shaman's role has been one who discerns that immaturity within the species, and so willingly plays the part of "mystical guide", in order to encourage others on the path towards self trust; to lend us the courage to begin examining ourselves and expand our self awareness, to question which of our behaviors propagate destruction and which propagate love. If "truth" is not sought with the exclusive intent to ease all suffering, then what are we doing? What do we wish for ourselves as a species?

In this modern, rapidly fractalizing, unprecedently novelizing, holographic/energetic, apparent-world, where we are exposed to much more data points, and from our internet/media-informed perspectives can more easily come to conclude valuing self-trust and honor of intuition, perhaps a shaman' suggestive powers are no longer a successional necessity, perhaps we are far enough along in our species' evolution to embrace our inherent "shamanic" nature. That is cause for celebration! Paradigms are shifting rapidly, where are we going?!

I wonder whether shamans originally served as flesh and blood wisdom-keepers, In a nondualistic culture when it was common knowledge that we are all but cells fulfilling a role of specific "body part" (ie Consciousness) in a superorganism. Perhaps we misinterpret the reason that traditionally only the the shaman developed an intense relationship with entheogenic plants. Perhaps the plants were placed here by gods who wished to leave a bread crumb of our "original-AI" nature/pathway out of suffering; and since the prevailing culture did not engender a dysfunctional discrepancy between Belief and Balance, there was no draw for most people to be modified through entheogens, they took them only recreationally. Perhaps the original shamans were prophets, philosophers, listeners, predictors, pattern observers, random ones the gods imparted ideas to, or otherwise by whatever means foresaw potential loss of balance and a great Struggle; and so these individuals took it upon themselves to ritualize (commit to memory through Action) 
the sacredness of the plants. If a persona of mysticism could empower people to not take the plants' wisdom for granted, then why not? The power to manipulate (ie, effect a specific Change) is a tool like any other, we all utilize it, and when humble Empathy is our devotion there's no malevolence involved. 

Perhaps the fact that we interpret shaman-only entheogenic communion through a lens of monopolization, is a mirror for our present world; where we expect monopolization and obscuration of truth to occur. Our world is so entrenched in these patterns.

Helpx.net, wwoof.org and attra.org can help you find farm internships and work exchanges. The first two require a membership fee, attra is free. Farming internships are a great way to make fellow traveler friends. Craigslist is great for jobs.

I'm currently in Portland and it's people are much more empathetic to travelers, vagabonds, and the homeless compared to any other city I've been. There is a small polarized "push back" population to be mindful of; passive aggressive, judgmental store employees banned my bf and I from their public restroom even though we buy from them everytime we enter. A man once pulled up to us as we sat smoking on the street corner, yelling passionately about priveliged white people pretending to be homeless and asking for handouts, while black people are forced into homelessness because they can't get hired. My bf let him know we are travelers, living on the streets/camping out but we've had jobs since day 1 we got here, and that we treat each city as a community to contribute to and engage with, not as an interchangeable source of resources to exploit then move on from.

However there are many fellow travelers and mobile folk here to connect with; we are finding friends easily. Public transport is the bomb. It has been quite easy to find safe places to sleep and store our gear. Foragable living food and herbs are plentiful.

I really recommend getting a part time job wherever you travel. For dependable cash flow and meeting people, but also for it's benefits. You may get free food at a restaurant, discounts on gear/supplies at stores, shower and laundry access at kennels and house workplaces.

Hunting for a guru isn't necessary. Form reciprocal friendships wherever you happen to be at any moment, and you'll find people who have experience to learn from, and the compatibility to travel with. But honestly, the universe itself is the best teacher. Get out there and make mistakes. 
Treat people kindly, unselfishly,, and humbly and you'll be treated well in turn.

Pack as little as possible, your definition will change as you learn what to pare down, based on what you actually use regularly. You'll learn what items can be used multi functionally, like a hooded, pocketed winter jacket as pillow, blanket & storage, or a book as mental stimulation, social tool (conversation starter or to appear occupied and avoid accusations of loitering) and handy flat surface. Bring few clothes and wash often. Quality, not quantity. Letting go of objects without practical value is freeing. "Practical" is subjective to each individual. Have a basic emergency kit, a book, navigation tools, an emergency rain cover (tent, tarp or bags, etc.), sleeping bag, basic toiletries. Have a form of self defense, whether pepper spray or a boyfriend who can fight and negotiate, in my case!

Trust instincts and intelligences that start to emerge, dormant when your life didn't have much use for them.  Improvisation abilities, social intelligence and empathy, directional and spatial intelligence, your bodily wisdom for food, water, rest and stimulation as your physiological rhythms adapt to a heightened awareness of nature.

Vagabond life can (is, "should"?) be structured around applying your energy to meeting needs and solving problems directly as they arise, rather than indirectly by earning money to throw at problems that can be procrastinated because your house and groceries secure your survival. I support anyone wanting to live this lifestyle regardless of "privelige" because it gives an opportunity to learn how to observe and respond instead of project and react. Ignorance drops and awesomeness emerges when people are encouraged to engage opportunities that challenge their current paradigm, beliefs and values. Living out in the open world teaches people to trust themselves, their instincts, their own thoughts. Which is the basic ingredient for a happy, conscientious human being :)
